prompts.prompt: Use case: compositing. Asset type: four local water-action sprite attachments for an existing game nest animation. Use the two reference water nests as the exact authority for turquoise color, creamy cyan highlight bands, dark teal outline, painterly polished cartoon material, lighting from upper left, and the same slightly top-down camera. Draw ONLY moving water masses, without the nest pool, rim, ground, bowl, text, grids, shadows or backgrounds. A genuinely transparent RGBA image. Arrange exactly four separate drawings in a strict 2 by 2 contact sheet with ample transparent margins. Each cell uses an identical 512-square coordinate frame and identical drawing scale; never zoom individual cells. Top left: anticipation, a thick low gathered water dome, 170px wide, centered at x256, bottom at y390, top near310. Top right: launch, a thick powerful curved water column surging straight up, base centered x256 y390, top near180, width110 to150, a round heavy tip, not a thin fountain spray. Bottom left: airborne peak, one substantial round water globule centered x256 y225 about140px wide and145px tall, a short tapering tail hanging downward, completely detached from the ground. Bottom right: landing impact, a broad stout crown splash at x256 y390, about250px wide, with two thick curling side lobes reaching up to y270 and a central depression, all connected, no tiny scattered droplets. These are usable animation attachment paintings, not preview mockups. Preserve reference material and clean continuous alpha contours. No sparkle flecks, grit, disconnected pixels, white matte or checkerboard.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: two COMPLETE separated water-nest animation layers, on true transparent RGBA. The attached approved water nest is the exact authority for design, perspective, turquoise palette, creamy cyan contours, dark teal shading and upper-left lighting. Create a strict 2-column 1-row parts board. Left cell: the LARGE LOWER POOL from the reference, with exactly its original broad organic oval silhouette, size, shape and bright curled front rim, but REMOVE the smaller rear upper basin and its connecting waterfall completely. Carefully paint the newly exposed rear-left lower-pool rim and calm oval water surface where the upper basin used to occlude them. This must be a complete natural closed pool with a curved continuous back rim, no polygon cuts, straight cut edges, empty notches, rectangular holes, floating slivers or rough matte. Keep all the visible lower-pool artwork as faithful to the reference as possible. Right cell: the SMALL UPPER BASIN ONLY, maintaining its reference appearance and rounded oval opening. Complete its entire underside, rounded sides and hidden back contour, as a clean independent thick bowl made of water. No waterfall stream hanging off it; the bowl's front must close continuously without a missing rectangle. These two parts will be reassembled and the upper bowl will physically jump upward, so their formerly hidden surfaces must be complete and polished. Keep the reference camera and drawing scale the same in both cells; don't enlarge the small basin to match the large pool. Generous transparent padding around both parts, no overlap, no text or guides, no ground or shadow, no tiny flecks. This is production layered source artwork, not a preview.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Production animation parts for the attached approved plant nest. Draw six isolated LEFT AND RIGHT FRONT PETAL PAIRS, in a strict 3-column by 2-row atlas, transparent RGBA. Only the two large creamy white and pale green front petals from the reference: do not draw the gold bean, green sprout, rear pointed leaves, ground leaves, side tendrils, base or ground. Each pair must be a COMPLETE layer down to the two meeting hinge roots, including hidden lower contours, so it can cover a fixed separate gold bean and fixed leaf base. Keep the exact painterly material, teal outline, rounded leaf anatomy, lighting from top left, same fixed frontal slightly top-down camera and equal drawing scale in all six cells. Both petals hinge together at the identical bottom center point, about (256,400) inside each 512-square cell. No canvas recentering or zoom. The top-left pair is fully closed: two tall rounded pointed cream petals meet at their upper tips, covering the central bean. Then row-major cell 2 begins to part at the tips, cell 3 opens one-quarter, cell 4 opens one-half, cell 5 opens three-quarters, and cell 6 is the exact wide curled OPEN pose of the approved reference front petals, including their curled inward tips. The pair bases stay together at the same hinge point and retain their volume and thickness throughout; the upper halves uncurl outward progressively. Preserve the gentle curved central seam in the closed pose. Ample transparent margins. No backgrounds, preview scene, text, grid lines, shadows, leaf-base fragments, dust, speckles or loose pixels.
